text:
Use Tier 2 architectural deepening: add learned relative-position biases to the existing MaskedRec attention layers. The latest macro HR@10 of 0.5363 remains below the recorded best of 0.5613, with Electronics still at 0.420. One plausible limitation is that absolute position embeddings alone make the network learn recency and relative ordering indirectly, especially across histories of different lengths.

The primary component to change is model_design. Add a trainable attention-bias table in each Transformer block, indexed by attention head and clipped signed distance between query and key positions. Add these biases to attention logits before softmax while preserving padding exclusion and bidirectional attention. This gives the endpoint mask a direct way to distinguish recent interactions from distant context, while signed distances preserve ordering for interior reconstruction. Initialize the biases to zero and retain the existing embeddings, reconstruction objective, negative sampling, and hyperparameters so this experiment isolates one architectural change.

The supporting component is training_evaluation: serialize the new parameters and update the predictor writer so validation and host inference instantiate the same architecture. Train one independent model per category with seed 42, retain the supplied splits and preprocessing seed 0, and select exactly one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10. Evaluate the change through the pinned host protocol and compare macro HR@10 against the recorded best, inspecting category scores to establish whether relative-position attention improves Electronics without sacrificing the other categories.
